motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing curve for movement and reveals.

motion.name: ui-transition
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border state changes.

motion.name: prism-fade
motion.purpose: Prism canvas fade-in once WebGL is ready.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition.

motion.name: line-on
motion.value: opacity + scaleY 0.9s var(--ease), staggered 70ms per line, once on entry
motion.purpose: Spectral rule lines light up red to violet like a forward pass.

motion.name: forward-pass
motion.value: every 7s or on click/tap, 13 scene units/s
motion.purpose: Pulse runs source -> glass -> lines, flaring each laminate plane.

motion.name: glass-sway
motion.value: yaw ±0.09 rad, pitch ±0.035 rad, small bob, pointer parallax

motion.name: light-glide
motion.value: arc (incidence ~34–64°); pointer height -> arc angle, horizontal -> radius; critically damped springs, ω 5.5 active / 1.2 idle
motion.purpose: The light glides along its arc and never snaps, even when the cursor jumps.

motion.name: light-breathe
motion.value: ±0.07 rad around the resting angle after 4s idle
motion.purpose: The idle light breathes in place instead of returning to a default spot.

motion.name: fresnel-fade
motion.value: Fresnel averaged over ±0.05 rad of incidence
motion.purpose: Lines fade over a couple of degrees at the onset of total internal reflection instead of blinking.

radiusMeta.micro-1: Neuron bars and the tops of spectral-rule lines.
radiusMeta.micro-2: Spectrum hit areas, sign-key swatches, progress bar, range tracks.

narrative.overview:
Xaytheon is an optical instrument, not a dashboard. The ground is a true-black viewing chamber; the chrome is white, grey and 1px hairlines; and the only colour anywhere is the visible spectrum, which only ever encodes data. A layer's hue is where it falls in the network, red at the input and violet at the output. Activations are light: a unit that fires harder glows from black through its hue to white. Cut units are black absorption lines. You hold the light, the model is a laminated glass prism, and its layers leave as a spectrum of discrete emission lines.

The system has two surface modes in one world. The landing persuades: a full-bleed laminated glass prism (three.js, real dispersion) that you steer by hand carries the hero, a live optics readout runs along its foot, a Spectral serif speaks the section titles, and the same twelve emission lines land flat on the page as the spectral rule. The lab operates: a dense three-pane instrument (input/output, inspector, layers) under a spectrum strip that spans the top, set in Geist with every number in Geist Mono. Density is high in the lab and generous on the landing; the materials never change between them.

It refuses grey dashboard panels, node-graph diagrams and glass panels. Depth comes from tonal steps of near-black and a single hairline weight, never from frosted surfaces or decorative colour.
keyCharacteristics: True-black ground (#000) with near-black tonal surfaces stepping up in 1–2% increments.
The visible spectrum is the only colour, and it is always data: layer position, activation, sign.
One hairline weight (1px) for every border and divider.
Spectral serif (300) for the wordmark and section titles only; Geist for UI; Geist Mono for every number.
White is the action colour: the primary button is the beam.
Restrained, slow optical motion on one easing curve; everything collapses under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Light Is Data Rule
rules.body: Spectral colour is never decoration. If a hue appears, it must answer "where in the network" or "how strongly did it fire". UI chrome stays black, white and grey.

rules.name: The Spectrum Only As Light Rule
rules.body: Fixed spectral colour appears only where the light itself is drawn: the twelve emission lines (hero prism and spectral rule) and the brand mark's three rays. Nothing else gets a hue that does not come from data.

rules.name: The One Hue Per Layer Rule
rules.body: A layer owns exactly one hue. Sign is shown by brightness and greying of that hue, never by borrowing a second colour (no red/blue diverging maps).

rules.name: The Absorption Line Rule
rules.body: A cut is shown as black: a black line in a spectrum, a heatmap dimmed to near-black (opacity 0.1–0.12) inside a dashed Smoke border, or a striped Smoke bar. Never a red "disabled" colour.

rules.name: The Mono Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any value an engineer might trust (counts, shapes, percentages, drift, coordinates, wavelengths) is set in Geist Mono with tabular numerals. Minus signs are true minus (−).

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Twice Rule
rules.body: Spectral appears only as the wordmark and section-level titles (plus the How-it-works step list on the landing). It never sets UI labels, buttons or data.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No frosted or blurred panels. A UI surface is opaque near-black; the only translucency is a black scrim laid over imagery or canvas.

dos: Do keep the ground true black (#000) and build depth with Soot, Graphite and Lit Graphite plus 1px hairlines.
Do derive every colour that carries meaning from wavelength via `src/viz/spectrum.ts`: red (680nm) at the input, violet (415nm) at the output.
Do render activations as emission (black → hue → white) and negatives as a grey shade of the same hue.
Do show cuts as black absorption: black lines, near-black dimmed maps, dashed Smoke borders.
Do set every number in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do use Spectral 300 only for the wordmark and section titles, with negative tracking.
Do make the primary action a Beam White button, one per view.
Do animate on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, keep UI transitions at 0.15s, and honour reduced motion.
Do use Lucide SVG icons at 13–18px, stroked, in currentColor.
Do keep errors and live indicators neutral (Graphite, Hairline Lit, Paper) and let an icon or a pulse carry the signal.
donts: Don't use spectral hues for decoration, brand accents, status or links; colour is always data (the brand mark's three rays and the twelve emission lines are the light itself, not accents).
Don't draw the light as a continuous rainbow gradient; it is always discrete emission lines.
Don't use diverging two-hue colour maps; one hue per layer, sign by greying.
Don't build grey dashboard panels or node-graph diagrams to explain a model; show it running.
Don't use frosted glass panels or backdrop blur; translucent black scrims over imagery and canvases (overlays, captions, tag chips) are part of the chamber and allowed.
Don't introduce a second border weight; every border and divider is 1px (the 2px focus ring and the 2px spectral-rule ticks are not borders).
Don't set UI labels, buttons or numbers in the serif, or set numbers in proportional figures.
Don't use uppercase tracked labels, kickers or eyebrows above titles.
Don't smooth heatmaps; they render pixelated.
